column10: This line?ôs original Alpha Beta Peel is touted as being the most popular product from Dr. Dennis Gross Skincare; now they offer their Extra Strength version. But even without the alcohol, the pH of 4.7 prevents the AHAs and BHA from functioning as exfoliants (a pH between 3 and 4 is ideal).Step 2, in both the original and Extra Strength Alpha Beta peels, are pads steeped in a solution of water with baking soda. Because step 2 is alkaline, it neutralizes the acids in step 1. However, you can neutralize any AHA or BHA product with plain tap water?îit doesn?ôt require special pads or a special solution.It?ôs a shame that both steps have a strong potential for unnecessary irritation and that they come packaged in jars. It?ôs even more of a shame for step 2 because it does contain an impressive assortment of anti-aging ingredients, but they won?ôt remain stable in the jar packaging. Not to worry, you can find these types of beneficial ingredients in many other products without any of the negatives.By the way, as to whether or not the Extra Strength Alpha Beta Peel is stronger than the original, it might be, but the company won?ôt reveal the differences in percentage so all you have to go by is the name. If you?ôre hoping to fight the signs of aging, this isn?ôt the way to do it.

If you have sensitive skin like me, you probably analyze your products on something like skin charisma to understand the ingredients and their purpose. Companies have been phasing out the plastic beads voluntarily with the Micro-Bead Free Waters Act in 2017. Some may still use them, so it is very important to read your labels. It?ôs also equally important to educate yourself on what it is you?ôre reading. You can?ôt determine whether cosmetic or personal care products contain plastic just by looking for an ingredient name on the label: Ingredients sharing the same name may be used as solid particles in one product or as a liquid in another.
